departments.name: Cardiology
departments.tagline: Heart checks, cath lab and cardiac rehab under one roof.
departments.summary: Complete heart care from ECG and echo to angioplasty, pacemakers and structured cardiac rehabilitation.
departments.imageAlt: A cardiologist reading an ECG trace with a patient
departments.heroAlt: A cardiology team reviewing a heart scan on a monitor
departments.overview: The Northcrest Heart Institute brings interventional cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists and rehab physiotherapists into one team. A 24/7 cath lab and a dedicated cardiac ICU mean a heart attack patient can go from the emergency door to an open artery in under 60 minutes.
procedures: Radial-access stenting with same-day discharge for most planned cases.
Device clinics follow you for life with remote monitoring.
2D/3D echo, TMT and stress echo reported the same day.
A 12-week supervised exercise and lifestyle programme after a heart event.
technology: Lower radiation and sharper images for complex procedures.
Detailed valve and chamber views without an invasive test.
faqs: Do I need a referral to see a cardiologist?
No. You can book directly online or at the OPD desk. Bring any previous ECGs, reports and your current medicines.
What should I do if I have chest pain?
Call our emergency line +91 80 4718 1000 or 108 immediately. Do not drive yourself. Chew a 300 mg aspirin if you are not allergic and a doctor has not told you otherwise.
How long is the stay after an angioplasty?
Most planned angioplasties through the wrist go home the same evening or the next morning. Emergency cases usually stay 2 to 3 days.
Is cardiac rehab covered by insurance?
Many policies cover the supervised sessions. Our TPA desk checks your cover before you start.

departments.name: Neurology & Neurosurgery
departments.tagline: Stroke-ready care for the brain, spine and nerves.
departments.summary: Stroke, epilepsy, headache, movement disorders and spine surgery with a round-the-clock stroke team.
departments.imageAlt: A neurologist examining a brain MRI scan
departments.heroAlt: Doctors reviewing brain scans on a large screen
departments.overview: Our neurosciences team treats conditions of the brain, spinal cord and nerves, from first seizures and migraines to strokes and complex spine surgery. A stroke code activates the emergency team, CT scanner and neurologist the moment a patient arrives.
procedures: Time-critical stroke treatment with a target of under 45 minutes door-to-needle.
Keyhole disc and decompression surgery with faster recovery.
Records seizures on video and brain activity together to guide treatment.
Day-care injections for chronic migraine and muscle stiffness.
technology: GPS-style guidance for precise brain and spine surgery.
EMG and NCS studies reported in 48 hours.
faqs: What are the warning signs of a stroke?
Remember BE FAST: Balance loss, Eyes (vision loss), Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call 108 or our emergency line.
Do I need an MRI before my first visit?
No. The neurologist will examine you first and order only the tests you need.
Is spine surgery always necessary for a slipped disc?
Most people improve with medicines and physiotherapy. Surgery is advised only when there is nerve weakness or pain that does not settle.
Can I drive with epilepsy?
Rules depend on how well seizures are controlled. Your neurologist will advise you and provide a fitness letter when it is safe.

departments.name: Orthopaedics
departments.tagline: Joint replacement, sports injury and trauma care.
departments.summary: Knee and hip replacement, arthroscopy, fracture care and physiotherapy to get you moving again.
departments.imageAlt: An orthopaedic surgeon reviewing a knee X-ray
departments.heroAlt: A physiotherapist helping a patient exercise their knee
departments.overview: From a sprained ankle to a full knee replacement, our orthopaedic surgeons and physiotherapists plan your care around one goal: getting you back to the activities you enjoy. Most joint replacement patients walk with support on the day after surgery.
procedures: Muscle-sparing techniques and an enhanced recovery pathway.
ACL reconstruction, meniscus repair and shoulder stabilisation.
24/7 trauma theatre for broken bones and complex injuries.
One-to-one sessions in our physio gym, plus a home exercise plan.
technology: Precise implant alignment for longer-lasting joints.
Ultra-clean air to lower infection risk in joint surgery.
faqs: How long does a knee replacement last?
Modern implants last 20 years or more for most people. Staying active and keeping a healthy weight helps them last longer.
How soon can I walk after joint replacement?
Most patients stand and walk with a frame on the day after surgery and go home in 3 to 4 days.
Do I need surgery for a ligament tear?
Not always. Partial tears often heal with bracing and physiotherapy. Your surgeon will discuss your activity level and goals.
Is physiotherapy included in the surgery package?
In-hospital physiotherapy is included. Outpatient sessions after discharge are billed separately or as a discounted bundle.

departments.name: Oncology
departments.tagline: Medical, surgical and radiation oncology with one tumour board.
departments.summary: Cancer screening, chemotherapy, surgery and radiotherapy planned together by a weekly tumour board.
departments.imageAlt: A patient receiving care in a calm oncology day-care unit
departments.heroAlt: An oncology nurse talking with a patient in the day-care unit
departments.overview: Every new cancer diagnosis at Northcrest is reviewed by a tumour board of medical, surgical and radiation oncologists, pathologists and radiologists. You get one written plan, one nurse navigator and a day-care unit designed for comfort during long treatments.
procedures: Given in a calm day-care unit with oncology-trained nurses.
Organ-preserving and minimally invasive operations where possible.
Image-guided treatment planned to protect healthy tissue.
Pain control, nutrition and counselling from day one.
technology: Whole-body scans to stage cancer and check response.
Safe, sterile preparation of every dose.
faqs: What is a tumour board?
A weekly meeting where specialists review your scans and biopsy together and agree one plan. You and your family then discuss it with your lead oncologist.
Can I get a second opinion?
Yes. Bring your reports and biopsy slides; our team usually reviews them within 5 working days.
Will I lose my hair during chemotherapy?
It depends on the medicines. Your oncologist will tell you before you start and our nurses can arrange scalp cooling where suitable.
Is cancer treatment covered by insurance?
Most health policies cover chemotherapy, radiotherapy and surgery. Our TPA desk handles pre-authorisation for you.

departments.name: Paediatrics & Neonatology
departments.tagline: Child-friendly care from newborns to teenagers.
departments.summary: Well-baby clinics, vaccinations, a level III NICU and paediatric specialists for every stage of childhood.
departments.imageAlt: A paediatrician gently examining a smiling child
departments.heroAlt: A paediatrician listening to a young child's heartbeat
departments.overview: Our children's wing has its own entrance, play areas and paediatric emergency room. Paediatricians, neonatologists and child specialists care for everything from routine vaccines to premature babies in our level III neonatal intensive care unit.
procedures: Full national and optional vaccine schedules with growth tracking.
Ventilation, phototherapy and kangaroo care for newborns who need extra help.
Children are seen by paediatric doctors, not adult teams.
Speech, occupational therapy and early intervention.
technology: Advanced ventilators and incubators with 1:1 nursing for the sickest babies.
Scopes, cannulas and monitors made for children.
Safe transfer of newborns from other hospitals.
faqs: Do you follow the national vaccination schedule?
Yes. We follow the IAP schedule and also offer optional vaccines. Bring your child's vaccination card to every visit.
Can parents stay with their child?
One parent can stay with a child at all times on the ward and in the NICU we encourage kangaroo care.
When should I bring my child to the emergency room?
Come straight away for breathing difficulty, a fit, a very drowsy child, a high fever in a baby under 3 months or signs of dehydration.
Do you have weekend clinics?
Yes. The paediatric OPD is open every day including Sundays and public holidays.

departments.name: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
departments.tagline: Pregnancy, birth and women's health at every age.
departments.summary: Antenatal care, high-risk pregnancy, natural and caesarean birth, fertility support and keyhole gynaecological surgery.
departments.imageAlt: An obstetrician performing a pregnancy ultrasound
departments.heroAlt: An obstetrician talking with an expectant mother
departments.overview: Our women's health team supports you from your first period problems to pregnancy, birth and menopause. Private birthing suites, a 24/7 obstetric theatre and our neonatal unit next door give you and your baby every safety net.
procedures: Scans, tests and doctor visits through all three trimesters.
Private suites with epidural pain relief available 24/7.
Keyhole removal of fibroids, cysts and hysterectomy.
technology: Every labour room is watched from the nurses' station.
Day-care diagnosis and treatment inside the womb.
faqs: When should I book my first pregnancy visit?
As soon as you have a positive test, ideally before 8 weeks. Your first visit includes a dating scan and blood tests.
Can my partner be present at the birth?
Yes. One birth partner can stay with you in the birthing suite, including for a planned caesarean in most cases.
Do you offer painless delivery?
Yes. Epidural pain relief is available 24/7 from our obstetric anaesthetists.
Is a Pap smear painful?
It may feel slightly uncomfortable but it is quick and not usually painful. It is recommended every 3 years from age 25.
